sources.title: Climate and Health Vulnerability Assessment: Sierra Leone
sources.organization: World Bank Group and Climate Investment Funds, with Sierra Leone Ministry of Health and Sanitation
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed climate data through 2020; hazard and health-system inputs from varying years; CMIP5 projections for the 2030s and 2050s.
sources.methodology: Assessment combines CRU observations, CMIP5 projections, and health/climate data.
sources.limitations: Health and administrative inputs are dated; the report notes limited drought surveillance and incomplete health statistics, so estimates are not current district monitoring.

sources.title: Disaster Risk Financing Strategy and Implementation Plan 2024-2029
sources.organization: Government of Sierra Leone, Ministry of Finance
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical disaster experience through 2022; strategy and implementation period 2024-2029.
sources.methodology: Government strategy compiles NDMA hazard calendars, prior risk assessments and historical disaster-loss data.
sources.limitations: Records are uneven; mapped hazards and losses are not climate-attribution estimates.

sources.title: Sierra Leone Common Country Analysis 2023
sources.organization: United Nations Country Team in Sierra Leone
geographic_coverage: Guinea and Liberia transboundary river basins
sources.temporal_coverage: Country conditions and climate-related sector risks summarized in the 2023 common country analysis; some historical conflict and migration context is included.
sources.methodology: UN Country Team multi-sector synthesis of country context, sector data, policy materials and climate-risk information.
sources.limitations: The analysis calls for better geographically and sex/age-disaggregated data; its climate annex is largely national and does not estimate local conflict effects.

sources.title: Multilateral peacebuilding in practice: addressing farmer-herder disputes along the border of Sierra Leone and Guinea
sources.organization: International Security and Development Center; Thissen et al.
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 research publication summarizing a UN Peacebuilding Fund-supported cross-border project and its evaluation.
sources.methodology: The accessible research summary reports satellite imagery, a household survey and qualitative interviews.
sources.limitations: Only the institute's article summary was accessible; detailed sample, effect sizes and subgroup results could not be checked in the full paper.

sources.title: Sierra Leone, Asset creation and livelihood: evaluation
sources.temporal_coverage: Asset creation and livelihood activities January 2020-December 2023; the page says evaluation fieldwork ran July 2023-July 2024.
sources.methodology: WFP publication page provides a summary of a decentralized evaluation of asset creation and livelihood activities.
sources.limitations: The page date predates its stated evaluation end date; only the online summary was accessible, with no district disaggregation or underlying sample details.

claims.locator: Printed p. 12, para. 23, and Figure 6 discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The assessment maps high-risk channels and coastal areas across Freetown; about 10 percent of residents are in high-risk zones, with Lumley, Juba, Susan's Bay and Regent wards at highest flood-fatality risk.
claims.scenario: Current risk estimate uses 2018 World Bank and UNDP hazard inputs.
claims.limitations: These are modeled risk estimates, not observed annual casualties or ward-level climate attribution.

claims.locator: Printed p. 15, para. 27 and Figure 8 discussion.
claims.paraphrase: For the 2050s, Koinadugu, Kono and Kailahun are projected to be the districts most vulnerable to drought, although the assessment estimates low countrywide likelihood of severe drought.
claims.scenario: CMIP5 projections for the 2050s under RCP 8.5.
claims.limitations: The report notes sparse drought surveillance; modeled district rankings are not observed future outcomes.

claims.locator: Printed p. 59, para. 90; printed p. 41, Table 6.
claims.paraphrase: A 2017 hazard system identified 81 of 1,317 health facilities at flood-inundation risk; Kailahun and Bombali had none, while Koinadugu had low reported health-worker density.
institutions: Hazard and Risk Profile Information System - Sierra Leone
claims.limitations: Facility exposure is based on 2017 mapping and workforce inputs are older; neither is a current district census.

claims.locator: PDF pp. 10-11 (one-based), Table 1 and following risk-assessment discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The government risk profile identifies Leicester, Regent, Granville Brook, Cline Town, Moa Wharf, Hill Court Road, Kissy Brook, Dwarzark and Charlotte in Western Area as landslide-prone under steep slopes and wet-season heavy rain.
affected_groups: residents of named Western Area locations
claims.limitations: The cited profile reports susceptibility and hazard locations, not a current site-by-site exposure count or climate attribution.

claims.locator: Printed p. 13, Section 2.1 and Figure 3 discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The strategy reports that 2015 and 2017 floods and landslides affected nearly 20,000 people and killed 1,141; 2017 Freetown events caused estimated damages of US$16.8 million and losses of US$14.9 million.
claims.limitations: The strategy aggregates disaster records and does not attribute these events to anthropogenic climate change.

claims.locator: Printed p. 19, Operational Framework; printed p. 25, Strategic Priorities.
claims.paraphrase: The strategy assigns disaster management from district and chiefdom committees through NDMA, gives local councils Level One response roles, and sets priorities for shock-responsive social protection and disaster financing.
claims.scenario: Government implementation priorities for 2024-2029; commitments are not evidence of completed delivery.
claims.limitations: The strategy documents planned mandates and priorities; it does not establish operational readiness or completed results.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 117-119, Annex 2, sections 'Disaster Preparedness and Management' and 'Water Resources'.
claims.paraphrase: The CCA describes recurrent seasonal and coastal floods inundating fields, roads and homes and contaminating water; severe drought dries streams and swamps relied on by rural poor households.
claims.limitations: This is a national synthesis; it does not quantify affected households or identify local hotspots in these passages.

claims.paraphrase: The CCA states that rural migration to Freetown during and since the civil conflict increased pressure on urban water resources; separately, shifting rainfall reduced river and stream flows and water access.
claims.limitations: The report does not say that climate caused conflict-related migration or estimate a causal effect of climate stress on conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The CCA links rural migration to Freetown during and since civil conflict with added pressure on urban water resources, while separately describing reduced flows under shifting rainfall; it does not claim climate caused the migration.

claims.locator: Accessible ISDC article summary and publication details.
claims.paraphrase: The study summary describes a Peacebuilding Fund project addressing farmer-herder conflicts on the Sierra Leone-Guinea border through climate-adapted agricultural livelihoods, peace messaging, border infrastructure and local dispute resolution; it reports effective agricultural components and perceived conflict reduction.
claims.limitations: The summary offers no effect sizes and only suggestive subgroup evidence; it does not state that climate caused the disputes. Full article access failed.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The summary explicitly places climate-adapted agricultural support within a project targeting farmer-herder conflict and strengthening local conflict resolution; it does not attribute conflict to climate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Accessible ISDC article summary, paragraph describing the project and paragraph summarizing results.

claims.paraphrase: WFP's public summary reports that Food for Assets and Integrated Village Solutions improved participation, financial inclusion and agricultural practices; it also reports improved food security and income generation among programme communities.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security
claims.limitations: The online summary provides no district-level results or sample detail; underlying evaluation PDF could not be opened.

claims.locator: Evaluation page, 'Key evaluation findings' and 'Key recommendations'.
claims.paraphrase: WFP's summary identifies irrigation maintenance, delayed inputs, land tenure and limited savings-group coverage as sustainability constraints and recommends stronger inclusion, local capacity, environmental management and resilience monitoring.
claims.limitations: These are summarized evaluation findings and recommendations, not district-specific performance estimates.

access_audit.reuse_terms: Report rights section encourages noncommercial dissemination with full attribution; no separate open license was verified.

access_audit.notes: Full public Government of Sierra Leone PDF text was accessible. Claims distinguish historical disaster records and mapped hazard susceptibility from climate attribution.

access_audit.reuse_terms: No separate reuse terms verified; license status remains unknown.

search_audit.query: Sierra Leone 2024 climate health vulnerability assessment district Koinadugu Kono Kailahun flood drought; Sierra Leone disaster risk financing strategy named hazard locations districts
search_audit.outcome: Found a detailed climate-health assessment with Freetown ward flood exposure, three interior drought-vulnerability districts and dated health-facility exposure; the government DRF strategy adds named Western Area landslide locations and national flood-loss records.

search_audit.query: Sierra Leone climate farmer herder conflict climate-adapted livelihood Peacebuilding Fund original evaluation; Sierra Leone climate conflict water migration common country analysis
search_audit.outcome: Found an accessible institute summary of a cross-border project combining climate-adapted agricultural livelihoods with farmer-herder conflict resolution, and a UN CCA account of conflict-era migration adding pressure to Freetown water resources alongside separate rainfall-related water stress. Neither source summary establishes that climate caused the conflict.

search_audit.query: Sierra Leone climate adaptation insecurity access conflict delivery project; Sierra Leone farmer-herder adaptation implementation violence disruption
search_audit.outcome: No inspected accessible source established that insecurity or organized violence stopped a named climate-adaptation activity. The ISDC summary describes a peacebuilding intervention addressing farmer-herder conflict, not conflict preventing adaptation delivery; the underlying journal article was inaccessible.

search_audit.query: Sierra Leone community climate adaptation resilience assessment district local government flood disaster preparedness primary report; Sierra Leone asset creation livelihood evaluation resilience smallholder farmers
search_audit.outcome: Found government district/chiefdom disaster-management roles, climate-health adaptation and early-warning gaps, and WFP-reported livelihood and asset-creation outcomes. WFP's underlying evaluation PDF was inaccessible, so resilience findings are limited to its public summary.

gaps: The subnational climate-health and facility evidence uses dated inputs, including 2017 facility exposure and 2016 workforce tables; current district-level monitoring was not located.

No accessible source found in the targeted searches documenting organized violence or insecurity halting a named climate-adaptation operation. Absence of such evidence in these searches is not evidence that disruption never occurs.
The UN CCA describes conflict-era rural migration and climate-related water stress in Freetown but does not estimate a causal relationship between climate change and conflict.
The 2026 farmer-herder study's full journal paper and the detailed WFP evaluation PDF were inaccessible; claims are limited to fully read publisher/institution summaries.
The WFP evaluation webpage date conflicts with its stated fieldwork period; the underlying report date and detailed evaluation evidence could not be independently reconciled.
